title: Wine Bug 59519: ole32 clipboard caches stale window handle — fix pending upstream
observation: Wine Bug 59519: ole32 clipboard caches stale window handle — fix pending upstream ## Summary Wine's OLE clipboard implementation (`dlls/ole32/clipboard.c`) caches the HWND from `get_clipbrd_window()` in a static local. When the STA thread that created the window terminates, the cached handle goes stale. The next `OleSetClipboard` call reuses the dead handle, `SendMessageW` targets a destroyed window, and clipboard operations silently fail. This affects any Proton game or application that creates and destroys STA threads with clipboard interaction (e.g. Space Engineers, AppID 244850). ## Fix A one-line `IsWindow()` guard before the cached-handle return in `get_clipbrd_window()`. If the cached window has been destroyed, the function falls through to the existing `!clipbrd->window` branch which creates a fresh one. - **Wine Bug:** https://bugs.winehq.org/show_bug.cgi?id=59519 - **Wine MR:**

title: why do games running in proton have access to the entire linux filesystem via Z:?
observation: why do games running in proton have access to the entire linux filesystem via Z:? Proton (all versions) creates a symlink to the machine's root `/` directory as `.../pfx/dosdevices/Z:` Why? This allows any game running in steam to trawl through my entire filesystem - with write access to any file where unix perms allow it.
